sections.title: Possession and reflexive reference: meaning and form
body: Goal: Describe who something belongs to and distinguish a person's own things from someone else's.
Core vocabulary: en ägare, en nyckel, en väska. Key phrases: Det är min jacka. · Hon tar på sig sin jacka. · Erik tvättar sin bil.

Use min/mitt/mina and din/ditt/dina with noun gender and number. Use hans, hennes and deras for another owner. Use sin/sitt/sina when the owner is the subject of the same clause: Lina tar sin cykel, but Lina tar hennes cykel means another woman's bicycle.
Say the examples aloud, notice the pattern, and then change one detail rather than memorising a fixed script.

examples.fi: Hon tar på sig sin jacka.
examples.en: She puts on her own jacket.

sections.title: Register, evidence and independent use
body: Register model: “Jag hittade dina nycklar.” is a neutral direct message way to express “I found your keys.”.
For listening and reading, answer from a specific word or phrase. For speaking and writing, make the recipient, purpose and next action clear.
Attempt the task before using the model. Improve one high-impact feature, then perform it again with the transfer condition.

assignment.title: Four-skill task and transfer
assignment.instructions:
LISTEN: First listen without a transcript. Answer: Where is Maja's phone? Replay once and identify the exact words that prove the answer.

READ: Read for purpose and evidence. Answer: Where are Amir's gloves? Mark the shortest phrase that supports your choice.

SPEAK: Describe three objects at home: say what each object is, whose it is and where the owner keeps it. Make a first attempt, check clarity and repeat once.

WRITE: Write a short lost-property message. Describe the item, say whose it is and explain where you found it. Check reader, purpose, required details and next action.

TRANSFER: A neighbour has taken your umbrella by mistake; explain which umbrella is yours and which is theirs.

BETWEEN LESSON · Optional, 5 minutes: retrieve the three key phrases without looking, then use one in a new sentence.
assignment.model: Det är min jacka. Hon tar på sig sin jacka. Erik tvättar sin bil.

takeaways: Notice: Use min/mitt/mina and din/ditt/dina with noun gender and number.
Transfer the pattern: A neighbour has taken your umbrella by mistake; explain which umbrella is yours and which is theirs.
